How to make a social video with Gemini, step by step (the hard way)

Gemini makes video clips right in the chat, and Flow builds scenes from them. A finished, posted video still needs an editor, captions, a cover and a scheduler. Here is every step, what it takes, and what it costs.
Gemini writes the script and generates the clips; Flow gives you more control over each scene.
You still need CapCut for the edit and captions, Canva for the cover and Buffer to post. Budget roughly 2¾ to 5 hours a video, and about $73 a month.
Or skip the stack: ask VEXI, and the video comes back cut, captioned and sized for each platform, then posted for you.

Of the big chat tools, Gemini has the most video built in. It writes, it makes images, and on paid plans it makes video clips in the chat. Google's newest model, [Gemini Omni](https://engadget.com/2176590/googles-gemini-omni-can-generate-anything-from-any-input-starting-with-video), launched on May 19, 2026, and makes and edits video by conversation.
Clips are not a finished social video, though. Below is the full route, from the script to a scheduled post. It works. It is the hard way, and you should know what it takes.

Prices are monthly billing, read on October 28, 2026, from each tool's own page unless a line says otherwise. They change often. The times are rough estimates for someone who knows the apps. Your first video will take longer. For ChatGPT or Claude, see [the ChatGPT guide](/blog/make-a-social-video-with-chatgpt) and [the Claude guide](/blog/make-a-social-video-with-claude).
Step 1: Write the script and the scene list in Gemini
**Cost:** [Google AI Pro](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) is $19.99 a month. AI Plus, at $4.99, now lists video in the Gemini app too, with fewer Flow credits. **Time:** about 15–30 minutes.

Ask for the script and the pictures at once. For example: “Write a 30-second voiceover for a vertical video about our spring sale at a garden shop. Hook in the first line. Short sentences. One call to action. Then split it into five scenes. For each scene, write a video prompt: the subject, the setting, the camera move and the light. No words in any scene.”
Read the script aloud with a timer. Each scene should match one or two lines of voice. Ask Gemini to tighten anything that runs long.
Step 2: Generate the clips in the Gemini app

**Cost:** included in your plan. Video in the Gemini app [needs a paid plan](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339). AI Pro includes a trial of Veo 3.1 Lite; AI Ultra, from $99.99, has full Veo 3.1. **Time:** about 30–60 minutes, most of it regenerating.

Paste the first scene prompt and ask for a vertical clip. Watch it. If the motion is wrong, say what to change in plain words: “slower camera, less sky, keep the pots in frame.” Omni edits by conversation, so you do not have to start over each time. Keep the best take, download it, and move to the next scene.

Two cautions. Generated video carries a [SynthID watermark](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339), Google's marker for AI-made content. And some reviewers [report spelling errors in the text of generated videos](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/gemini.google.com), so keep words out of your clips. Add text in the edit instead.
Step 3: Build matching scenes in Flow
**Cost:** included. [Flow credits](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) come with each plan: 200 on AI Plus, 1,000 on AI Pro, with Omni Flash. **Time:** about 30–60 minutes. This step is optional.

The Gemini app is quick. Flow, Google's filmmaking tool, [came to Workspace in January 2026](https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/01/flow-available-additional-google-service-workspace.html), and it is better when your scenes must look alike. Following [Google's Flow help](https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16894016): open a project and describe the scene. Click the model name and choose **Video**. Under **Ingredients**, add reference images, such as your product or your shop, so they show up in every clip. Under **Frames**, add a start or end image and describe the move between them. Set the aspect ratio to vertical, choose how many versions you want, and generate.
Use your own photos as ingredients. A clip of your real storefront beats a made-up one. Download the clips you keep.
Step 4: Edit and add the voice in CapCut
**Cost:** [CapCut Pro](https://www.capcut.com/pricing) is $19.99 a month on monthly billing; a no-cost tier has the basics. **Time:** about 45 minutes to 1½ hours.

Start a 9:16 project. Record the voiceover first, straight into CapCut on your phone, or import one from a voice tool such as ElevenLabs. That would be another bill. Lay the clips over the voice in order, then trim each one so the cut lands on a word. Generated clips often start or end with odd motion, so cut the first and last half-second. Add music well under the voice and check that the track is cleared for business use.
Step 5: Add captions and on-screen text

Captions let the video work with the sound off. In CapCut, generate auto captions from the voice track. Then read every line. Auto captions mishear names, prices and street names. Fix them by hand. Add the on-screen text from step 1 as separate text layers, kept clear of the bottom of the frame where each app puts its buttons. Export at 1080 x 1920. Export again for any other size you post.
Step 6: Make the cover in Canva and schedule it in Buffer

**Cost:** Canva Pro is about $18 a month ([as reported by Piktochart](https://piktochart.com/blog/canva-pricing-2026-costs-raised/); Canva's own page could not be read). [Buffer](https://buffer.com/pricing) Essentials is $5 a month per connected account, so Instagram, TikTok and Facebook come to $15. **Time:** about 25–35 minutes.
In Canva, make a 1080 x 1920 design. Drop in your best frame and a short title in big type, kept to the middle so profile grids do not crop it. Download it.

Gemini's [plans list no posting or scheduling](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) to your social accounts. So open Buffer, create a post, upload the video and the cover, paste the caption, adjust it for each platform, pick a time and schedule it. Then start the next video.
**Time:** add up the estimates and one 30-second video takes roughly 2¾ to 5 hours once you know the apps. Skip Flow and it is a little less. Regenerating clips and the edit are the biggest blocks.

**Money:** Google AI Pro $19.99, CapCut Pro $19.99, Canva Pro $18 and Buffer at $15 come to about $73 a month for four subscriptions. That is the cheapest of the common chat stacks; [Claude's](/blog/make-a-social-video-with-claude) is about $103.

And you are the glue. You write the prompts, regenerate the clips that came out wrong, edit, caption, design the cover, check each post and remember to post. Gemini makes beautiful seconds of video.
